title: Dynamical Tunneling Blockade in Layer-Pseudospin Ferromagnets
authors: Lingxian Kong, Yuta Murakami, Ryuichi Shindou, Zhiyuan Sun
abstract: Double-layer systems with narrow or flat electronic bands may exhibit spontaneous interlayer coherence, described by a layer-pseudospin ferromagnetic order parameter. In modern realizations of layer-pseudospin ferromagnets, the electrons carry additional valley degeneracies, endowing each layer with a valley-pseudospin degree of freedom. We study their nonequilibrium steady states driven by a static interlayer voltage bias in the presence of interlayer tunneling. While in the low-bias regime, the system is in a static state with parallel valley pseudospins between the two layers, we show that in the high-bias regime, the dynamical precession of the layer-pseudospin stabilizes the valley pseudospins in the antiparallel configuration, strongly suppressing the interlayer tunneling. This dynamical tunneling blockade leads to an absence of ac current and a sharp drop of the dc tunneling current to a tiny value, in stark contrast to conventional quantum Hall double layers.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes how interlayer tunneling in layer-pseudospin ferromagnets behaves under an applied voltage bias. The key finding is that when valley degeneracy is present, high bias drives the system into a dynamical tunneling blockade. This blockade suppresses the DC current, providing a distinct signature compared to simpler, valley-less models.
main_problem: The study investigates the non-equilibrium steady states of layer-pseudospin ferromagnets driven by an interlayer voltage bias, focusing on the role of valley degeneracy.
main_result: In the presence of valley degeneracy and high bias, the system undergoes a dynamical tunneling blockade, forcing the valley pseudospins into an antiparallel configuration, which sharply suppresses the DC tunneling current.
method: The analysis employs the Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert (LLG) equation for the layer-pseudospin, coupled with spinor equations and Green's function techniques to calculate current response functions.
model_or_system: The system is a double-layer ferromagnet with narrow bands, modeled by layer-pseudospin and valley-pseudospin order parameters. The dynamics are governed by an energy functional including anisotropy, polarization, and Josephson tunneling terms.
key_observables: Interlayer tunneling current density ($I(t)$), DC tunneling current ($I_{dc}$), and the time-averaged valley overlap ($\langle Z angle$).
important_parameters: Interlayer voltage bias ($\mu$), valley anisotropy strength ($K$), and the tunneling amplitude ($c_0$).
main_assumptions: The LLG equation is used for dynamics, and approximations involve separating slow evolution from fast oscillations, as well as using Green's function techniques for current calculation.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the $I_{dc}$ vs. bias ($\mu$) characteristics for both valley-less and valley-degenerate cases, showing the transition to blockade in the latter. Other figures show the effective gauge potential and time-averaged valley overlap.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the LLG dynamics for the layer-pseudospin, then incorporating valley degrees of freedom, and finally analyzing the high-bias regime to derive the condition and consequences of the dynamical tunneling blockade.
why_interesting: The interplay between spin/pseudospin dynamics (LLG) and charge transport (tunneling current) in a correlated electron system is highly relevant to understanding novel electronic states in 2D materials and topological systems.
